In [[number theory]], '''cuspidal representations''' are certain [[group representation|representations]] of [[algebraic groups]] that occur discretely in <math>L^2</math> spaces.{{sfnp|Cogdell|Kim|Murty|2004|loc=lecture 2, section 5}} The term ''cuspidal'' is derived, at a certain distance, from the [[cusp form]]s of classical [[modular form]] theory. In the contemporary formulation of [[automorphic representation]]s, representations take the place of [[holomorphic function]]s; these representations may be of [[adelic algebraic group]]s.

When the group is the [[general linear group]] <math>\operatorname{GL}_2</math>, the cuspidal representations are directly related to cusp forms and [[Maass form]]s. For the case of cusp forms, each [[Hecke eigenform]] ([[newform]]) corresponds to a cuspidal representation.

== Formulation ==
Let <math>G</math> be a [[reductive group|reductive algebraic group]] over a [[number field]] <math>K</math> and let <math>\mathbb{A}</math> denote the [[adele group|adele]]s of <math>K</math>.  The group <math>G(K)</math> embeds diagonally in the group <math>G(\mathbb{A})</math> by sending <math>g</math> in <math>G(K)</math> to the tuple <math>(g_p)_p</math> in <math>G(\mathbb{A})</math> with <math>g=g_p</math> for all (finite and infinite) primes <math>p</math>. 

Let <math>Z</math> denote the [[center of a group|center]] of <math>G</math> and let <math>\omega</math> be a [[continuous (mathematics)|continuous]] [[character (mathematics)|unitary character]] from <math>Z(K)\setminus Z(\mathbb{A})^\times</math> to <math>\C^\times</math>.
Fix a [[Haar measure]] on <math>G(\mathbb{A})</math> and let <math>L^2_0(G(K)\setminus G(\mathbb{A}),\omega)</math> denote the [[Hilbert space]] of [[complex number|complex]]-valued [[measurable function]]s <math>f</math> on <math>G(\mathbb{A})</math> satisfying
#<math>f(\gamma g)=f(g)</math> for all <math>\gamma\in G(K)</math>, 
#<math>f(gz)=f(g)\omega(z)</math> for all <math>z\in Z(\mathbb{A})</math>,
#<math>\textstyle\int_{Z(\mathbb{A})G(K)\,\setminus\, G(\mathbb{A})} |f(g)|^2\,dg < \infty</math>,
#<math>\textstyle \int_{U(K)\,\setminus \,U(\mathbb{A})}f(ug)\,du = 0</math> for all [[unipotent radical]]s <math>U</math> of all proper [[Borel subgroup|parabolic subgroups]] of <math>G(\mathbb{A})</math> and <math>g\in G(\mathbb{A})</math>.
The [[vector space]] <math>L^2_0(G(K)\setminus G(\mathbb{A}),\omega)</math> is called the '''space of cusp forms with central character {{math|''ω''}}''' on <math>G(\mathbb{A})</math>. A function appearing in such a space is called a '''cuspidal function'''. 

A cuspidal function generates a [[unitary representation]] of the group <math>G(\mathbb{A})</math> on the complex Hilbert space <math> V_f</math> generated by the right translates of <math>f</math>. Here the [[Group action|action]] of <math>g\in G(\mathbb{A})</math> on <math>V_f</math> is given by
:<math>(g \cdot u)(x) = u(xg), \qquad u(x) = \sum_j c_j f(xg_j) \in V_f.</math>
The space of cusp forms with central character <math>\omega</math> decomposes into a [[direct sum of Hilbert spaces]]
:<math>L^2_0(G(K)\setminus G(\mathbb{A}),\omega) = \widehat{\bigoplus}_{(\pi,V_\pi)} m_\pi V_\pi</math>
where the sum is over [[irreducible representation|irreducible]] [[subrepresentation]]s of <math>L^2_0(G(K)\setminus G(\mathbb{A}),\omega)</math> and the <math>m_\pi</math> are positive [[integer]]s (i.e. each irreducible subrepresentation occurs with ''finite'' multiplicity). A '''cuspidal representation of {{math|''G''(}}'''<math>\mathbb{A}</math>'''{{math|)}}''' is such a subrepresentation <math>(\pi, V_\pi)</math> for some <math>\omega</math>.

The groups for which the multiplicities <math>m_\pi</math> all equal <math>1</math> are said to have the [[multiplicity-one property]].
